entries.userBenefit: Spending effort as you generate it means your output never exceeds your rate. Storing it behind a latch lets one release exceed anything you could do live.
entries.mechanismConnection: Stomatopod raptorial appendages are loaded against a saddle-shaped exoskeletal spring retained by a latch, releasing stored elastic energy far faster than muscle could contract.

entries.title: Cold Hand Against Warm Hand
entries.objective: Thunnus thynnus keeps its swimming muscle, viscera, eyes and brain well above the water around it, using counter-current exchangers that trap metabolic heat instead of losing it at the gills. Warm muscle contracts and recovers faster, warm viscera digest faster and fund the rate, warm eyes and brain keep reactions sharp in cold water. Together they open feeding grounds most large fish cannot use. Its principle is Ocean Heat. The metaphor? Keep your own heat in.
entries.animalRule: The cold hand goes first and both hands do exactly the same task with the same objects, timed on the clock.
entries.userBenefit: You lose most of your capability by letting heat leak out - sleep, food, warmth, recovery - and then blame your discipline. Feeling the difference in your own hands makes that trade impossible to ignore.
entries.mechanismConnection: Thunnus thynnus retains metabolic heat with counter-current vascular exchangers, holding muscle, viscera, eyes and brain above ambient so contraction, digestion and reaction all stay fast in cold water.

entries.title: Collect Five Snacks Moving Only Below Cover
entries.objective: Gather five snacks placed around a room while staying below the height of the furniture and keeping contact calls going with a partner.
entries.animalRule: Your head must stay below the top of the furniture, and every pickup must be followed by a call and an answer.
entries.userBenefit: A playful game that keeps two people in touch without needing to see each other.
entries.mechanismConnection: Red-backed Fairywren — Rhythmic • Cover-tied • Foraging: Malurus melanocephalus groups forage steadily through grass and low shrubs, staying mostly inside cover and keeping in constant touch with soft contact calls. This Trial translates that cover-tied foraging with running contact calls into collecting snacks while staying low and trading whistles with a partner.

entries.title: Collect One Useful Thing Everyone Missed
entries.objective: During one shared activity, notice and collect one useful leftover, forgotten resource or overlooked opportunity that would otherwise be wasted.
entries.animalRule: Works a penguin colony on foot all day, taking spilled krill, eggs, carrion and waste. Keep that true for the whole attempt.
entries.userBenefit: Trains resourcefulness and leaves the user with value recovered from something others ignored.
entries.mechanismConnection: Snowy Sheathbill expresses Polar Opportunism through this mode: Snowy Sheathbill — Colony-Edge Krill Theft — Walking • Intercepting • Constant: Works a penguin colony on foot all day, taking spilled krill, eggs, carrion and waste. The Trial carries that same limiting structure into one concrete human action.

entries.title: Collect Ten Nuts Only When Both Signals Show
entries.objective: Gather ten nuts into a cup, moving only when a helper's food sign and safe sign are up together.
entries.animalRule: One nut per overlap, and any nut moved outside an overlap goes back to the bowl.
entries.userBenefit: A fast, funny timing game that rewards patience over grabbing.
entries.mechanismConnection: Hazel Dormouse — Foraging • Timing-led: Muscardinus avellanarius forages at night in the shrub layer, feeding on flowers, insects, berries and hazelnuts as each comes into season, so its active weeks are timed to when food and safety overlap. This Trial translates that foraging only when food and safety line up into ten nuts moved only while two separate signals overlap.

entries.title: Collect Twenty Pegs in a Rolling Line
entries.objective: With two or three others, collect twenty scattered pegs along a strip by leapfrogging from the back of a file to the front.
entries.animalRule: Only the rearmost person moves, always to the front: the file rolls forward together.
entries.userBenefit: A quick group game that makes a boring tidy-up fun.
entries.mechanismConnection: Snow Bunting — Rhythmic • Grounded • Circuit: Flocks of Plectrophenax nivalis forage across open snowy ground in a rolling movement, with birds at the back flying over the flock to land at the front where the seeds are fresh. This Trial translates that rolling flock where the back birds leapfrog to the front into twenty pegs collected by a leapfrogging line of people.

entries.title: Collect, Do Not Compose
entries.objective: A Hwamei does not have a song so much as a collection. It learns phrases from the other birds around it, folds them into long varied sequences, and keeps adding through its life, so any individual's repertoire reflects the particular scrub it grew up in and no two birds sing the same set. Originality by accumulation rather than invention. Its principle is Borrowed Song. The metaphor? Stop trying to invent it. Collect enough from around you and the combination is already yours.
entries.animalRule: Exactly five elements must come from five different sources, each credited, and they have to be combined into one thing rather than listed.
entries.userBenefit: Waiting to invent something original is why you have produced nothing. Five collected pieces combined is genuinely yours, takes an afternoon, and nobody else has that combination.
entries.mechanismConnection: Garrulax canorus acquires song phrases from surrounding birds throughout life and incorporates them into long individually distinctive sequences, so repertoires vary continuously with local acoustic environment.

entries.title: Colour a Paper Spider to Match a Leaf
entries.objective: Colour a small paper spider to match one real leaf so closely that it almost disappears when laid on it.
entries.animalRule: Match this one leaf's exact green: the spider wins only if it blends with that surface.
entries.userBenefit: A calm little art task that trains your eye for colour.
entries.mechanismConnection: Green Huntsman Spider — Still • Blended • Poised: Micrommata virescens is coloured by a green pigment that matches the leaves it rests on, letting it sit still in plain view on foliage while prey and predators fail to see it. This Trial translates that leaf-matched green body held still on foliage into one paper spider coloured to vanish on a chosen leaf.

entries.title: Colour in Living Skin
entries.objective: The blue in a booby's feet is carotenoid pigment it cannot make and gets only from fish, and carotenoids are also drawn on by the immune system, so a bright foot means an animal both eating well and with some to spare. Crucially the colour sits in living skin rather than a feather, so it is not a record of last year, and experiments have found feet dulling measurably within days of poor feeding. Its principle is Blue-Foot Signal. The metaphor? Use a signal that reflects your current state, not your history.
entries.animalRule: The replacement must reflect current state rather than history, and the historical signal has to be set aside during the attempt.
entries.userBenefit: A signal based on your history keeps earning you credit you no longer deserve, and people discover that at the worst moment. Current state never has that problem.
entries.mechanismConnection: Sula nebouxii foot colour derives from dietary carotenoids held in living skin and competes with immune allocation, dulling measurably within days of reduced food intake.

entries.title: Colour One Paper Flatfish Into the Floor
entries.objective: Colour a flat paper fish to match a patterned floor or rug so closely that a helper spots a plain control fish on the same patch but misses yours.
entries.animalRule: Both fish lie fully in the open with nothing on top of them: only colour and pattern may hide yours.
entries.userBenefit: A quiet colouring puzzle that trains your eye for tone and pattern.
entries.mechanismConnection: European Plaice — Flat • Hidden • Patient: Pleuronectes platessa lies flat on the seabed and adjusts the pigment cells in its upper skin to match the tone and pattern of the sand or gravel beneath, so its whole body reads as ground to a passing predator or prey. This Trial translates that pigment-matched flat body into a paper fish coloured to disappear on one patch of floor.

entries.title: Colour Only at the Right Angle
entries.objective: A male Swinhoe's pheasant is not coloured the way a parrot is. Most of what looks blue-black on him is structural: layered nanostructure in the feather barbules returning particular wavelengths, which means the colour exists only at the angles where that light reaches an eye. In the closed shade of Taiwanese broadleaf forest he reads as a dark shape; turn him into a shaft of light and it appears. Its principle is Cautious Color. The metaphor? Build something that only becomes visible from the angle you choose to present.
entries.animalRule: The visibility must depend on a condition you control during the attempt, and it may not be continuously on display.
entries.userBenefit: Anything continuously on display is assessed when you are not ready. Making it appear only on your condition means it is only ever seen at its best.
entries.mechanismConnection: Lophura swinhoii iridescent plumage arises from multilayer nanostructure in the barbules, so the colour is angle-dependent and absent under diffuse forest shade.

entries.title: Colour With No Pigment At All
entries.objective: A sunset moth breaks two moth conventions at once: it flies by day, and its colour contains no pigment at all. The wing scales are built as curved ribbed lattices that reflect particular wavelengths by interference, so the colour shifts with viewing angle and is far more intense than any pigment could produce, and it costs the insect nothing to maintain once grown. Its principle is Iridescence. The metaphor? Build the effect into the structure once, and it costs nothing to keep afterwards.
entries.animalRule: The effect must be structural and require no ongoing upkeep during the attempt, and the repeated production has to stop.
entries.userBenefit: Producing an effect repeatedly means it stops the moment you do. Building it into the structure once keeps it going for nothing.
entries.mechanismConnection: Chrysiridia rhipheus wing colour arises from structural interference in ribbed scale lattices rather than pigment, requiring no metabolic maintenance after development.

entries.title: Comb a Lawn in Line for Ten Caps
entries.objective: Walk a patch of lawn shoulder to shoulder with at least one partner, sweeping gloved hands through the grass to find ten bottle caps a non-searching helper has hidden.
entries.animalRule: Stay in line: nobody breaks away to search alone, and the line only turns together.
entries.userBenefit: A cooperative search that turns a patch of ground into shared teamwork.
entries.mechanismConnection: Cownose Ray — Aligned • Gliding • Forage-line: Rhinoptera bonasus travels in coordinated schools that glide low over sand, funnelling it with their lobes to uncover buried shellfish while many eyes share the watch for sharks. This Trial translates that coordinated line sweeping sand for buried prey into a shoulder-to-shoulder sweep that finds hidden bottle caps together.

entries.title: Comb Out What Is Suspended
entries.objective: The inside edges of a duck's bill carry lamellae, rows of fine comb-like ridges, and in the dabbling ducks they form a working sieve. The Hottentot Teal draws water in at the tip and the tongue pumps it out through the sides, while the lamellae retain small invertebrates and seeds suspended in it. It never sees the food; it filters the medium. Its principle is Ebbing-Marsh Dabbler. The metaphor? You keep hunting for items. Pass the whole medium through a filter and keep what sticks.
entries.animalRule: The filter must be set before you start rather than applied by judgement as you go, and everything not matching it has to pass through untouched.
entries.userBenefit: Judging each item as it arrives is what makes a feed exhausting and leaves you with nothing. One filter set in advance lets the whole flow pass and you keep only what you meant to.
entries.mechanismConnection: Spatula hottentota draws water in at the bill tip and expels it laterally using the tongue as a pump, with fine bill lamellae retaining suspended invertebrates and seeds from the flow.

entries.title: Comb Tide-In Confetti With an Anchored Hand
entries.objective: With your elbow fixed on a table, comb falling paper confetti out of the air with spread fingers only while a helper calls tide in, until twenty dots are in the cup.
entries.animalRule: Your elbow stays cemented to its mark, you comb only while the tide is in, and your hand is a closed, still fist whenever it is out.
entries.userBenefit: A playful, rhythmic catching game in letting the flow bring the work to you.
entries.mechanismConnection: Acorn Barnacle — Rhythmic • Tidal • Attached: Semibalanus balanoides cements itself permanently to rock and, when the tide covers it, sweeps its feathery legs through the water in a steady rhythm to comb out food, closing its plates when the tide goes out. This Trial translates that fixed, rhythmic combing only while the tide is in into sweeping spread fingers through falling confetti from an anchored elbow on called tides.

entries.title: Come Ashore All at Once
entries.objective: Kemp's ridley is a crab specialist for most of its life, crushing blue crabs on shallow Gulf bottoms. Reproduction runs on a completely different rhythm: nesting is concentrated on the Tamaulipas coast at Rancho Nuevo, where females come ashore together in synchronised mass landings called arribadas, unusually in daylight and often in strong winds. Arriving together is the protection. Its principle is Mass Beach Landing. The metaphor? Arrive together, not one at a time.
entries.animalRule: Everyone must act at the same moment, and nobody may go first alone.
entries.userBenefit: Raising something alone when others want the same thing means you absorb the whole reaction and they wait to see how it goes. Everyone arriving at once means nobody is the one exposed.
entries.mechanismConnection: Lepidochelys kempii nests in synchronised daytime arribadas concentrated at Rancho Nuevo, with mass simultaneous emergence swamping predators.

entries.title: Come Back and Rearrange It
entries.objective: A male satin bowerbird builds a structure that is not a nest and will never hold an egg. Two parallel walls of upright sticks form an avenue, the inner faces painted with chewed plant material applied with a wad of bark, and in front of it he arranges a collection of blue objects: feathers, flowers, bottle tops, drinking straws. He maintains it for months and rearranges constantly. What is displayed is not strength but sustained discrimination, which is what the female is assessing. Its principle is Curation. The metaphor? Taste, maintained for months.
entries.animalRule: All ten objects share one colour, the arrangement is revisited at least twice, and each revisit has to change it rather than confirm it.
entries.userBenefit: Doing something impressive once tells people nothing, because anyone can manage one burst. Returning to it repeatedly is what shows the judgement you actually have.
entries.mechanismConnection: Ptilonorhynchus violaceus constructs and continuously maintains an avenue bower painted with masticated plant matter and decorated with blue objects, advertising sustained discrimination rather than physical condition.

entries.title: Come Back to the Same Crevice
entries.objective: The European spiny lobster has no claws at all. Its defence is a spined carapace, long spined antennae and one particular crevice, and the crevice is the part it works at. Individuals occupy the same caves and overhangs for years, forage out at night and return to the identical shelter. For an animal that matures at five and may live decades, a known refuge is worth far more than a new one. Its principle is Red Armor. The metaphor? Return to the shelter you already know.
entries.animalRule: It must be a shelter you have genuinely used before, and no improved alternative may be substituted.
entries.userBenefit: Looking for a better version of what already steadied you means you spend the hard weeks searching instead of recovering. Going back to the known one works immediately because you already know it does.
entries.mechanismConnection: Palinurus elephas shows strong den fidelity, returning after nocturnal foraging to the same rocky crevice over multiple years in the absence of claws.

entries.title: Come Down for the Salt
entries.objective: A Scarlet Macaw can fly tens of kilometres in a morning and open seeds nothing else can, which makes it look like the freest animal in the forest. It is not. On many mornings hundreds of parrots come down to one specific exposed face of riverbank clay and eat the soil, and the evidence points to sodium, which is vanishingly scarce in the western Amazon. All that range still depends on a few clay banks. Its principle is Colorful Labor. The metaphor? Range is not independence. Know which few places you actually depend on.
entries.animalRule: No more than three dependencies may be named, and at least one must get a concrete protective action today rather than being noted for later.
entries.userBenefit: Being busy everywhere hides the two or three things everything actually rests on, so you never protect them. Naming them takes ten minutes and tells you exactly where a bad week would come from.
entries.mechanismConnection: Ara macao travels widely but aggregates at specific exposed riverbank clay licks to ingest soil, with evidence indicating sodium acquisition in a region where dietary sodium is extremely scarce, tying a wide-ranging bird to a few fixed sites.

entries.title: Come Out on the Light, Not the Hour
entries.objective: A Nephrops lives in a mud burrow and leaves it on no clock at all. Emergence is triggered by how much light reaches the seabed, so the same species comes out at dawn in shallow water, around midday in the deep, and continuously in the darkest conditions. Reading the real condition rather than the hour is what keeps it fed and unexposed. Its principle is Burrow Watch. The metaphor? Let the condition decide, not the hour.
entries.animalRule: The trigger must be an observable condition, not a time, and the action waits until that condition is genuinely present.
entries.userBenefit: Running your day on the clock means you act when the conditions are wrong and blame yourself for the poor result. Naming the real trigger puts the effort where it actually works.
entries.mechanismConnection: Nephrops norvegicus times burrow emergence by the intensity of light reaching the seabed, so the same population emerges at dawn in shallow water and at midday in deep water.

entries.title: Come Out When It Is Mild
entries.objective: The speckled padloper only forages when conditions are mild, and especially after winter rain has brought up small succulents and annual plants, taking most of its water from juicy leaves. Through the heat and drought it stays in the rocks and does nothing. The activity is entirely conditional, and the condition is checked before the animal commits. Its principle is Minishell. The metaphor? Only go out in the mild window.
entries.animalRule: The check must happen before committing, and an unfavourable check has to produce no demanding activity at all.
entries.userBenefit: Pushing a demanding thing through unfavourable conditions produces a poor version you then have to redo and tells you nothing about your ability. Checking first spends the effort where it lands.
entries.mechanismConnection: Chersobius signatus forages only in mild conditions, especially after winter rains, obtaining most of its water from succulent leaves.

entries.title: Come Up for Air on Purpose
entries.objective: The West African lungfish has gills and still cannot live by them. Adults depend on paired lungs and must rise to the surface to gulp air, so an active predator in a swamp full of water has to interrupt its hunting to breathe, again and again, all season. The breath is not a break from the work; it is a condition of doing it at all. Its principle is Mud-Cocoon Survival. The metaphor? Build the breath into the work.
entries.animalRule: The interval must be fixed in advance and kept even when the work is going well, and the breaks have to be real stops.
entries.userBenefit: Skipping breaks when the work is flowing is exactly when you need them, and the collapse comes hours later disguised as something else. A fixed interval you keep regardless is what makes a long stretch survivable.
entries.mechanismConnection: Adult Protopterus annectens are obligate air breathers with reduced gill function, surfacing repeatedly to ventilate paired lungs even while actively hunting.

entries.title: Common in the Shop, Gone at Home
entries.objective: The Bala Shark is one of the most familiar aquarium fish in the world and is close to gone from most of the rivers it came from. It is a large cyprinid that shoals in fast-flowing channels and needs far more space and current than almost anyone provides, and wild populations fell sharply from the 1970s. Abundance where you see it says nothing about abundance where it lives. Its principle is Group Harmony. The metaphor? Check the source, not the shelf.
entries.animalRule: The ten minutes must go on the source rather than the product, and you have to state the finding plainly even when it turns out to be unremarkable.
entries.userBenefit: Seeing something everywhere makes you assume it is plentiful, which is exactly how shortages surprise you. Ten minutes on the source tells you whether your supply is actually safe.
entries.mechanismConnection: Balantiocheilos melanopterus is ubiquitous in the aquarium trade while wild populations in Borneo, Sumatra and Thailand have declined severely, so commercial abundance is decoupled from the status of the species in its native rivers.

entries.title: Compare Fizz in Cold and Warm Glasses
entries.objective: Pour sparkling water into a chilled glass and a warm glass at the same time and watch which keeps its gas.
entries.animalRule: Both glasses must be poured at the same moment so the only difference is temperature.
entries.userBenefit: A one-minute kitchen experiment that shows why cold drinks stay fizzy.
entries.mechanismConnection: Crocodile Icefish — Cold • Transparent • Steady-flow: Chionodraco hamatus has no red blood cells or haemoglobin and carries oxygen dissolved in its clear plasma, which works only because near-freezing water holds much more dissolved gas and a large heart moves a big blood volume slowly through wide vessels. This Trial translates that dependence on cold water holding more dissolved gas into a side-by-side pour of cold and warm sparkling water.

entries.title: Compare the Inside and the Outside
entries.objective: Locating a sound means comparing two receivers, and the usual cues are useless to an animal a centimetre across. Crickets solved it differently: the eardrums on each front leg are joined to each other and to thoracic spiracles by an air-filled tube, so sound reaches each membrane from both outside and inside, and the two paths interfere. The direction comes from comparing internal against external. Its principle is Dusk Wing-song. The metaphor? Compare what you are hearing outside with what you already know inside.
entries.animalRule: Both the external account and your own internal knowledge must be stated, and the action has to follow from the difference during the attempt.
entries.userBenefit: Acting on an outside account alone is why you keep being surprised. Comparing it against what you already know usually shows you exactly where it is wrong.
entries.mechanismConnection: Gryllus bimaculatus tympana are acoustically coupled via a tracheal tube to thoracic spiracles, so each membrane receives sound externally and internally and directionality arises from the interference between the two paths.

entries.title: Complete the Cycle Without Going to Sea
entries.objective: Most sturgeons are anadromous: they grow in the sea and return to fresh water to spawn, which makes them vulnerable at both ends and at every barrier in between. The Siberian Sturgeon does not go to sea at all. It completes its entire life inside one great river system, so no dam, estuary or coastal fishery sits across its path. Fewer transitions, fewer places to be cut off. Its principle is Deep Patience. The metaphor? Every handoff is somewhere it can break. Complete it inside one system.
entries.animalRule: At least two handoffs must be removed and the work completed within a single system, with nothing passed out and back.
entries.userBenefit: Every handoff is a place your thing stalls for days waiting on somebody. Completing it inside one system usually finishes today what would otherwise take you a fortnight.
entries.mechanismConnection: Acipenser baerii is potamodromous, completing its entire life cycle within the Siberian river systems rather than migrating to sea, avoiding the estuarine and coastal transitions other sturgeons depend on.

entries.title: Confirm the Distance, Then Fire
entries.objective: A red slender loris spends its night creeping, testing each branch before loading it and adjusting its position by millimetres. All of that is preparation for a single fast accurate grab: once the path is confirmed safe and the distance to an insect is known precisely, the hand moves faster than anything about the animal suggests. Speed is only permitted after certainty. Its principle is Slow-Branch Caution. The metaphor? Earn the right to move fast by confirming the distance first.
entries.animalRule: No fast movement may occur before the confirmation during the attempt, and the distance has to be confirmed rather than estimated.
entries.userBenefit: Moving fast before you know the distance means missing and being left somewhere you cannot hold. Confirming first is what makes the quick move land every time.
entries.mechanismConnection: Loris tardigradus tests each support and fixes prey distance through slow deliberate positioning before executing a rapid accurate manual strike.

entries.title: Contact Area, Not Glue
entries.objective: A tokay gecko holds a vertical pane of glass with no glue and no suction. Each toe pad carries millions of fine hairs branching into hundreds of finer tips, and when those tips come within a few nanometres of a surface the molecular attraction between them is enough to hold the animal. The strength is entirely about how much of it is genuinely touching. Its principle is Grip Voice. The metaphor? You are not failing to commit hard enough. You are barely in contact. Increase the touching surface.
entries.animalRule: At least three separate small contacts must be made, and no single large effort may substitute for them.
entries.userBenefit: One big push at something you are losing grip on does not stick and exhausts you. Three small contacts hold far better and cost you almost nothing.
entries.mechanismConnection: Gekko gecko toe pads bear millions of setae branching into hundreds of spatulae each, generating adhesion through van der Waals forces proportional to true contact area rather than suction or secretion.

entries.title: Contact Only Pays When They Are Crowded
entries.objective: A wood stork holds its bill open in the water and sweeps it slowly side to side, and when anything brushes the inside it closes faster than any decision. That works in water too muddy to see through, but it has a condition: contact only happens often enough to be worth the effort when fish are crowded. In a full marsh they are spread thin and the bird gets nothing. Its principle is Sensitivity. The metaphor? Wait for the concentration.
entries.animalRule: The density must be verified before starting during the attempt, and the method may not be used in thin conditions.
entries.userBenefit: Running a contact method in thin conditions means you work all day for nothing and start doubting the method. Verifying density first is a five-minute check for you.
entries.mechanismConnection: Mycteria americana feeds by tactolocation, snapping the open bill shut on contact in turbid water, which requires high prey density and fails when fish are dispersed.

entries.title: Contest One Better Spot Without Touching
entries.objective: Win the better of two places using position alone.
entries.animalRule: No contact of any kind; a touch forfeits the spot immediately.
entries.userBenefit: Three seconds of genuine competition that costs nothing and nobody gets hurt.
entries.mechanismConnection: Goliath Beetle — Larva Builds, Adult Spends — Sap-fed • Contesting • Short-lived: An adult that cannot grow at all runs on sap and fruit sugar through a brief season of flying, fighting over feeding sites and breeding, spending a body that a larva spent months assembling out of rotting wood and protein This Trial translates that brief adult season spent contesting feeding sites into a no-contact race for the better spot.

entries.title: Continuous Beating, No Rest
entries.objective: The cost of a razorbill's wing is that flight requires continuous rapid beating with no glide, so every metre in the air is paid for at full rate. The bird accepts that because the same wing works underwater. There is no efficient cruising mode at all; the design has only two states, both expensive, and the diving is what justifies it. Its principle is Dual Mastery. The metaphor? Accept that one capability has no cheap mode, and price the rest of your day around that.
entries.animalRule: The honest cost must be stated, and the rest of the day has to be planned around it rather than around a hoped-for reduction during the attempt.
entries.userBenefit: Hoping something expensive will get cheaper means planning a day that does not work. Pricing it honestly once means the rest of your day actually fits.
entries.mechanismConnection: Alca torda wing loading permits no gliding flight, so aerial transit requires continuous high-frequency flapping, a cost accepted in exchange for underwater propulsion capability.

entries.title: Contribute and Lose One
entries.objective: A guira cuckoo group builds one nest and several females lay into it, which sounds cooperative until you watch what happens next: females throw out eggs already there, and chicks that hatch behind the others are frequently killed. The same group then shares incubation, feeding and the noisy mobbing which is what keeps predators off a nest none of them could defend alone. Cooperation and sabotage run through the same structure at once. Its principle is Scruffy Alliance. The metaphor? The cost buys the protection.
entries.animalRule: A genuine contribution has to be made and one of your own items genuinely given up to common use, both today.
entries.userBenefit: Expecting a shared arrangement to cost you nothing means you leave the first time it does, and lose the protection too. Accepting one loss keeps the whole thing working.
entries.mechanismConnection: Guira guira breeds communally with joint incubation and predator mobbing while females eject each other's eggs, so cooperation and sabotage operate within the same nest.

entries.title: Converge on a Shared Signature
entries.objective: African greys live in flocks that change composition constantly, roosting in large numbers and dispersing into smaller feeding parties. Managing that requires knowing who is who, and the parrot does it through vocal learning: individuals produce and copy specific calls, converging on shared signatures that let birds locate and address particular companions rather than broadcasting at everyone. Its principle is Mimic Intelligence. The metaphor? Learn and use the individual's own signature rather than broadcasting to the group.
entries.animalRule: The address must use the individual's own phrasing during the attempt, and no general broadcast may be used.
entries.userBenefit: Broadcasting to a group means nobody feels addressed and your message is ignored. Using someone's own phrasing means they answer you.
entries.mechanismConnection: Psittacus erithacus learns and converges on shared contact call signatures with specific individuals, permitting addressed rather than broadcast communication within fission-fusion flocks.

entries.title: Converge on an Unrelated Butterfly
entries.objective: This butterfly shares its biology with the other longwing in its genus and it would be wrong to manufacture a difference: both take pollen as adults, live for months, learn fixed flower circuits and are genuinely distasteful. What is specific is who it looks like, because across its enormous range it converges on the wing pattern of a second unrelated longwing, so predators learning one are deterred from both. Its principle is Signal Memory. The metaphor? Converge on the signal of someone unrelated who is making the same claim, and the learning is shared.
entries.animalRule: The other party's claim must be genuinely the same during the attempt, and convergence has to be deliberate.
entries.userBenefit: Inventing your own signal means teaching every predator separately and paying for it. Converging with someone making the same claim halves the cost for both.
entries.mechanismConnection: Heliconius melpomene converges on the wing pattern of the unrelated co-mimic Heliconius erato across their shared range in a Mullerian mimicry ring.

entries.title: Converge Three Hands on One Landmark on Time
entries.objective: Agree one fixed landmark and an exact minute with two others, then all three arrive from different places and lay a hand on it within one minute of that time.
entries.animalRule: The landmark stays put and everyone comes to it from a separate, distant starting point, at the agreed minute.
entries.userBenefit: A tiny, dependable meet-up that gets three people in the same place.
entries.mechanismConnection: Orange Roughy — Aggregating • Spawning • Seamount-bound: Hoplostethus atlanticus gathers at particular times of year in dense, predictable aggregations over seamounts and slope features to spawn, so the fixed feature and the season bring scattered fish together. This Trial translates that timed convergence on one fixed seafloor feature into three people arriving from different places to lay hands on one landmark at an agreed minute.

entries.title: Convert a Muscle Into a Heater
entries.objective: Cold slows down eyes. A retina at ten degrees registers changes far more sluggishly than one at twenty-five, which is a serious problem for a predator chasing fast fish into deep water. Billfish solved it by converting one of the muscles that would normally move the eye into a heat-producing organ instead, packed with mitochondria and dedicated to warming the eyes and brain. Its principle is Open-Water Drive. The metaphor? Repurpose something you already have into the support your main capability needs.
entries.animalRule: The repurposed thing must stop doing its original job during the attempt, and it has to genuinely support the main capability.
entries.userBenefit: Keeping everything doing its original job means your main capability is unsupported where it matters. One repurposing costs you a minor function.
entries.mechanismConnection: Makaira nigricans has a modified superior rectus eye muscle converted into a mitochondria-rich thermogenic organ that warms the retina and brain during deep cold-water pursuit.

entries.title: Convert What Others Reject
entries.objective: A Water Buffalo is usually described by what it endures, and the more useful description is what it converts. Its rumen breaks down coarse high-fibre material more completely than a cow's, so it thrives on rice straw that would not maintain cattle, and more people drink its milk than any other dairy animal's. Converting the rejected input is the whole advantage. Its principle is Resilience. The metaphor? Toughness is not grinding. Take what others discard.
entries.animalRule: Every main input must be something that was genuinely about to be discarded, shown as waste first. The result has to be actually used or eaten, not just presented.
entries.userBenefit: You read resilience as putting up with more, which just costs you. The version that pays is being able to use the input everyone else writes off, because that supply is cheap and nobody is competing for it.
entries.mechanismConnection: Bubalus bubalis carries a rumen microbial population that digests coarse high-fibre forage more completely than cattle can, letting it be maintained on rice straw and crop residue, and its wide splayed mobile-jointed hooves spread weight across ground that would bog machinery.

entries.title: Cook One Thing Over Outdoor Heat
entries.objective: Cook one simple food outdoors using an already-established legal cooking fire or grill.
entries.animalRule: Use one steady heat source and judge progress from repeated visible changes rather than constantly changing the setup.
entries.userBenefit: Turns heat-reading into a concrete outdoor cooking challenge.
entries.mechanismConnection: House Cricket expresses Hearth Rhythm through this mode: Produces sound by drawing a toothed file on one forewing across a scraper on the other, and because the muscles driving that stroke run on temperature-dependent chemistry, the chirp rate rises and falls with the warmth of the room closely enough to be read as a thermometer. The Trial carries that same limiting structure into one concrete human action.

entries.title: Cool It Without Spending
entries.objective: A Beira lives on bare Somali rock with no shade and no standing water, and never drinks. Its oversized thinly furred ears carry a dense network of blood vessels that radiates heat straight out of the blood, a way of cooling that costs no water at all. Shedding heat for free is what makes the whole animal possible there. Its principle is Rock Mastery. The metaphor? Stop paying for comfort. Use surface, not supply.
entries.animalRule: No ice, no water, no fridge or freezer at any point. Only spreading, pouring, exposing surface or moving air may be used, and the drop has to be visible or stated.
entries.userBenefit: Your first instinct for a problem is to spend something on it. Solving it with surface and airflow instead costs nothing and keeps working when the thing you would have spent runs out.
entries.mechanismConnection: Dorcatragus megalotis has very large thinly furred ears with an extensive surface network of blood vessels that radiates heat directly from the blood, a waterless form of cooling essential to an animal that does not drink and takes all moisture from plants.

entries.title: Cool One Drink Without Adding Water
entries.objective: Cool One Drink Without Adding Water.
entries.animalRule: No ice or refrigeration may be used during the attempt.
entries.userBenefit: You turn tiny thermoregulation into one concrete experience with a visible finish.
entries.mechanismConnection: Kirk's Dik-dik — Browsing • Waterless • Nose-cooled: An elongated flexible snout with a dense blood supply is pumped like a bellows so that evaporation inside it cools blood on its way to the brain, which lets the animal survive without drinking. This Trial translates that mechanism into one drink by evaporative wrapping.

entries.title: Cool One Work Setup
entries.objective: Change one small work or rest setup to reduce heat load using shade, airflow, lighter covering, or a cooler contact surface, then photograph before and after.
entries.animalRule: Make exactly one heat-management change and preserve the setup's original function rather than abandoning it for a different location.
entries.userBenefit: Produces an immediately useful comfort improvement by adapting several small heat pressures instead of relying on brute endurance.
entries.mechanismConnection: Zebu's relevant mechanism is: Combines a larger surface area, a more reflective coat, denser sweat glands and lower heat production, so it stays functional in conditions where temperate cattle stop feeding and stop producing

entries.title: Cool Only the Part That Cannot Take It
entries.objective: Sweating removes heat well and spends water badly, so a Sahel oryx does the opposite: it lets its body temperature climb through the day, storing heat in its tissue, and sheds it at night when the air is cooler than the animal. The brain cannot tolerate that, so a carotid rete cools blood on its way up against venous blood from the nasal passages. Its principle is Oryx Return. The metaphor? Protect only the part that cannot run hot.
entries.animalRule: Only one thing may be protected during the attempt, and the rest has to be genuinely allowed to degrade rather than quietly maintained.
entries.userBenefit: Protecting everything in a hard stretch means you protect nothing properly and lose the one that mattered. Choosing one is how you come out intact.
entries.mechanismConnection: Oryx dammah stores metabolic heat by allowing body temperature to rise, while a carotid rete cools arterial blood against venous blood returning from evaporatively cooled nasal passages to protect the brain.

entries.title: Copy One Hidden Word After Ten Dark Minutes
entries.objective: Let your eyes adapt to near-darkness until you can read and copy a word you could not make out at first.
entries.animalRule: No extra lights, screens or moving closer, and the helper stays silent: only patience and fully adapted eyes read the word.
entries.userBenefit: A calm ten minutes in the dark that shows how much your own eyes can recover.
entries.mechanismConnection: Giant Squid — Drifting • Watching • Concealed: Architeuthis dux has among the largest eyes of any animal, letting it drift at low energy cost in the dim deep sea while picking up faint, distant cues such as the glow of disturbed luminous plankton. This Trial translates that patient watching with eyes built for faint light into copying one hidden marker word read by a single faint light after ten minutes of adaptation.

entries.title: Copy One Skilled Move Exactly
entries.objective: Learn one small technique by observation before improvising your own version.
entries.animalRule: You must learn by watching and reproduce the technique first, echoing Sumatran Orangutan stick-tool use learned socially for defended fruit.
entries.userBenefit: You gain one concrete micro-skill and practise observation before premature improvisation.
entries.mechanismConnection: Sumatran Orangutan — Stick Tools for Defended Fruit — Tooling • Social • Deliberate: Makes and uses sticks to extract seeds from fruit protected by stinging hairs, a technique learned by watching rather than invented This Trial translates that species-specific mechanism into one observed useful technique.

entries.title: Copy One Striped Pattern Down Two Separated Chains
entries.objective: Let one black, white and chestnut stripe pattern drift into two different forms by copying it down two chains that never see each other.
entries.animalRule: The river is never crossed: the first copy on each bank sees only the original, and every later copy sees only the one before it on its own bank, never the other bank.
entries.userBenefit: A calm drawing game that shows, on the table in front of you, how groups that stop mixing slowly turn different.
entries.mechanismConnection: Prevost's Squirrel — Populations separated by rivers and straits • Each isolated block diverging in coat colour: across Sundaland, Callosciurus prevostii populations appear to be separated by large rivers and sea straits that a canopy squirrel rarely crosses, and the black, white and chestnut coat pattern differs between these blocks, giving dozens of described regional forms. This Trial translates that divergence of a shared pattern in separated populations into two copying chains split by a string river, where small unintended copying changes pile up separately on each bank.

entries.title: Copy One Trend Then Change It
entries.objective: Learn one current content format by imitation, then publish your own visibly changed version.
entries.animalRule: First acquire the recognizable local pattern by imitation; only then produce your own rendition of it.
entries.userBenefit: Uses social imitation as a learning mechanism while still requiring an original transformation.
entries.mechanismConnection: Common Hill Myna expresses Borrowed Voices through this mode: Learns its calls only from same-sex neighbours in a small area, producing sharp local dialects while never imitating other species in the wild, so the celebrated mimicry appears only when there are no conspecifics to copy. The Trial carries that same limiting structure into one concrete human action.

entries.title: Copy the Feature They Check
entries.objective: Birds identify a wasp by specific features, so the Wasp Moth reproduces exactly those: transparent wings, a narrow banded abdomen, clubbed antennae. It is not a general impression of waspiness. It is a targeted copy of the small number of things the receiver actually examines. Its principle is Hornet Costume. The metaphor? Stop polishing what nobody inspects. Find the feature they check and nail that.
entries.animalRule: The checked feature must be found out by asking or observing rather than assumed, and only that feature may be improved during the attempt.
entries.userBenefit: You polish the parts you enjoy and the decision turns on something you never touched. Finding out what they actually check takes one question and redirects all your effort to where it counts.
entries.mechanismConnection: Arctiine wasp moths reproduce the specific diagnostic features avian predators use for recognition, rather than general resemblance, concentrating mimetic investment where receiver attention falls.

entries.title: Copy the Veins, Not Just the Colour
entries.objective: This Florida species is one of the largest katydids in North America and uses a far simpler disguise than the lichen and moss mimics: it just looks like a green leaf. Its long broad forewings extend well past the abdomen and carry a strong central vein with a network of finer ones, so perched motionless it has the outline, the colour and the venation of the leaves around it. Its principle is Leafvein. The metaphor? Copy the internal structure too.
entries.animalRule: A structural element must be matched rather than an appearance, and the rebuild has to be done today.
entries.userBenefit: Copying the look of something good without its structure gives you a version that falls apart under use, and you blame yourself rather than the copy. Matching one structural element is what makes it hold.
entries.mechanismConnection: Stilpnochlora couloniana bears elongate forewings with a pronounced median vein and reticulate secondary venation reproducing broadleaf foliage structure.

entries.title: Copy Yourself Until It Turns
entries.objective: When conditions are good a water flea does not bother with males at all: females produce daughters that are genetic copies, and the population multiplies at full speed with no partner needed. Only when the water deteriorates does it switch to sexual reproduction and resting eggs. Cloning while it works, recombining when it stops. Its principle is Clone Until Crisis. The metaphor? While something is working, just repeat it. Save the reinvention for when it stops.
entries.animalRule: Nothing may be changed or improved during the repeat, and the thing has to be one that is demonstrably working rather than one you hope will.
entries.userBenefit: You reinvent things that are working because repeating feels lazy, and the variation usually makes them worse. Repeating exactly is the cheapest output you will ever get.
entries.mechanismConnection: Daphnia pulex reproduces by apomictic parthenogenesis in favourable conditions, producing genetically identical daughters at high rate, and switches to sexual reproduction with resting eggs only when conditions deteriorate.

entries.title: Correct in the Air, Land Somewhere Safe
entries.objective: A satin flycatcher launches at an insect before the outcome is settled, adjusts its line mid-flight as the target moves, and then turns straight back into cover. The sally only works because the correction happens while airborne and the return is already decided; a bird that committed to one trajectory would miss and be exposed. Its principle is Quick Perch Turn. The metaphor? Commit before it is certain, correct while moving, and know where you are landing.
entries.animalRule: The correction must happen during the movement rather than before it in the attempt, and the landing position has to be chosen in advance.
entries.userBenefit: Waiting for certainty before committing means the thing has gone, and committing without a chosen landing leaves you stranded. Correcting on the way is what makes going early safe.
entries.mechanismConnection: Myiagra cyanoleuca sallies from a perch and adjusts its flight trajectory mid-air to intercept moving insects before returning directly to covered perching.

entries.title: Correct One Bent-Line Aim
entries.objective: Place a coin or target behind a clear glass of water and compare where it appears from two angles, then mark the corrected line of sight.
entries.animalRule: Use observation only; the corrected mark must be based on two viewing angles rather than moving the target to match your first guess.
entries.userBenefit: Makes refraction tangible and trains the habit of correcting perception when the apparent position differs from the real one.
entries.mechanismConnection: White-throated Kingfisher uses this mode by strikes at where a submerged fish actually is rather than where it appears to be, correcting for refraction at whatever angle it is looking from, which is a different calculation on every dive

entries.title: Cost Almost Nothing While Waiting
entries.objective: Between meals a Burmese Python's metabolic rate falls so low that a very large animal costs almost nothing to maintain, which is why months without food are unremarkable for it. The waiting is not endurance, it is cheapness. An animal that is expensive to run cannot afford to wait for the right opportunity. Its principle is Giant Pressure. The metaphor? If waiting costs you a lot, you will take a bad offer. Get your waiting cheap.
entries.animalRule: The cost of waiting must be stated as a specific figure or quantity, and one real reduction has to be made today rather than planned.
entries.userBenefit: When waiting is expensive you take the first offer rather than the right one. Cutting the running cost of waiting buys you the ability to hold out, which is usually worth more than the offer itself.
entries.mechanismConnection: Python bivittatus suppresses standard metabolic rate profoundly between feeds, with reduced organ mass and digestive activity, so maintenance costs fall low enough that intervals of months between meals are routine.

entries.title: Count Coins a Sticky Note Holds Two Ways
entries.objective: Measure how many coins one sticky note holds when the load drags along the surface and how many when it peels straight away.
entries.animalRule: Same note, same bag, coins added one at a time: only the direction of the pull changes, along the surface first and then straight away from it.
entries.userBenefit: A ten-minute measurement that shows why some tape holds a poster up yet still peels off cleanly.
entries.mechanismConnection: Madagascar Day Gecko — Running up glass • Holding • Peeling off in one direction: Gecko toes carry millions of branching setae that stick by intermolecular attraction, so the grip engages when pulled along a surface and releases with almost no force when peeled away from it. This Trial translates that direction-dependent grip into one sticky note loaded along a surface and an identical note loaded straight away from it, with the coins counted each time.

entries.title: Count the Gap
entries.objective: A Platypus dives with its eyes, ears and nostrils shut and reads two signals at once: the electric field of a moving shrimp, which arrives almost instantly, and the pressure wave, which takes measurable time. The gap between them scales with distance, and that is what lets it range prey it will never see. Its principle is Integration. The metaphor? One signal tells you nothing. Two, and the delay between them, tells you where. Count the gap.
entries.animalRule: You must use both the sight of the clap and the arrival of the sound, and say your guess out loud before pacing it out. The distance has to be long enough that a gap is audible.
entries.userBenefit: A single reading leaves you guessing. Two imperfect signals plus the lag between them locates a thing precisely, which is how you get position out of information that looked useless alone.
entries.mechanismConnection: Ornithorhynchus anatinus hunts with eyes, ears and nostrils closed, using tens of thousands of electroreceptors and a comparable number of mechanoreceptors in its bill; the electrical field of moving muscle arrives before the pressure wave, and the delay between them encodes distance.

entries.title: Count the Sneezes First
entries.objective: Lycaon pictus does not decide to hunt individually. The pack performs a greeting rally first - sneezing, circling, excited contact - and the hunt begins only when enough animals have joined in; studies found the number of sneezes predicts whether the pack actually goes. The decision is collective and it is what makes a relentless pursuit possible, because a half-committed pack cannot hold the pace. Its principle is Pack Relentlessness. The metaphor? Count the yeses before you start.
entries.animalRule: Every person gives an explicit spoken yes or no, silence counts as a no, and the thing does not start without a full set of yeses.
entries.userBenefit: Starting group things on assumed agreement is why they fall apart halfway and you end up carrying them. One round of explicit yeses takes two minutes and tells you whether to start at all.
entries.mechanismConnection: Lycaon pictus packs decide collectively through a sneeze-punctuated greeting rally, and the hunt only begins once enough individuals have joined the display.

entries.title: Count What You Lost Too
entries.objective: A jay forgets a great many of its acorns, and that is not a failure of the system. Every one it forgets has been buried at the right depth away from the parent tree, which is why oak woodland spreads at the speed a jay flies. The bird is paid in the ones it remembers and the forest is paid in the ones it does not. Its principle is Memory. The metaphor? Some of your losses planted something.
entries.animalRule: Ten items, nothing written down, recall attempted only at the end of the day, and anything not recalled is left in place rather than hunted for.
entries.userBenefit: Measuring yourself only by what you remember hides how much of your effort pays off elsewhere. Seeing what you lost and what it became changes how you count the day.
entries.mechanismConnection: Garrulus glandarius caches thousands of acorns annually and the unrecovered fraction, buried at viable depth away from parent trees, is a primary dispersal route for oaks.

entries.title: Cover It With What Is Already There
entries.objective: A long-nosed bandicoot has a short life and little margin, and by day it rests in a shallow scrape heaped over with leaves and grass gathered from immediately around it. The nest is invisible not because it is hidden somewhere clever but because it is made of exactly what the surrounding litter is made of. Local material is what makes it disappear. Its principle is Soilwork. The metaphor? Cover it in the local material.
entries.animalRule: Only material already in use locally may be used, and the rebuild has to be completed today.
entries.userBenefit: Bringing in a format from elsewhere makes your work the thing people react to rather than its content. Rebuilding the surface from what they already use gets the content looked at instead.
entries.mechanismConnection: Perameles nasuta rests in a shallow scrape roofed with leaves and grass collected from the immediate surroundings, matching the local litter.

entries.title: Cover One Stretch at Almost No Cost
entries.objective: Travel a distance letting something else do the work, and watch while you go.
entries.animalRule: Your own effort may not drive the movement, and nothing may be in your hands for the whole stretch.
entries.userBenefit: You see a piece of your commute properly, probably for the first time in years.
entries.mechanismConnection: Steppe Eagle — Soaring, wide and opportunistic: broad wings on thermals cover enormous distances of open steppe at almost no cost, taking ground squirrels, following locust swarms and dropping onto carrion as it appears. This Trial translates that free distance into a stretch travelled unpowered with the eyes doing the work.

entries.title: Crack a Bowl of Walnuts for Everyone
entries.objective: Do the heavy opening work so everyone else in the house can simply eat.
entries.animalRule: You do the opening and others do the eating: the bowl goes out for the household before you take any yourself.
entries.userBenefit: A bowl of fresh walnuts for the house and a quiet, satisfying quarter hour of cracking.
entries.mechanismConnection: King Vulture — Soaring above canopy • Following smaller vultures down • Tearing the hide open: The king vulture has no keen sense of smell and follows the smaller smelling vultures down to a carcass, then uses a bill heavy enough to tear through the hide that they cannot open, after which everyone present can feed. This Trial translates that heavy-billed opening of what others cannot get into into cracking a full bowl of hard-shelled walnuts for the household.

entries.title: Crack It at the Back of the Jaw
entries.objective: A snail shell is a good defence because breaking it usually costs more than the animal inside is worth, and swallowing it whole means carrying a stomach full of indigestible carbonate. A caiman lizard solves both halves. Its rear teeth are broad, blunt and molar-like, set at the back of the jaw where the closing muscle has most leverage, and the shell is cracked against a wide bony palate rather than swallowed. Its principle is Crushing Niche. The metaphor? Apply force where your leverage is greatest, and discard the packaging rather than carrying it.
entries.animalRule: The point of greatest leverage must be identified before applying force, and the unwanted part has to be discarded during the attempt.
entries.userBenefit: Applying force where the problem presents itself means fighting it at your weakest point. Moving to your leverage makes the same effort break it.
entries.mechanismConnection: Dracaena guianensis has broad molariform posterior teeth positioned at the point of maximum adductor leverage and crushes snail shells against a wide bony palate, expelling the shell.

entries.title: Cradle an Open Bowl Still as Pompoms Drift
entries.objective: Hold a wide bowl completely still for ten minutes while a helper lets pompoms drift down at random, catching only those that fall in.
entries.animalRule: The bowl never moves toward a pompom: only what drifts into it counts.
entries.userBenefit: Ten calm minutes of stillness with a gentle game attached.
entries.mechanismConnection: Pelican Eel — Drifting • Coiled • Patient: Eurypharynx pelecanoides hangs almost motionless in the dark deep sea with its huge mouth ready, spending as little energy as possible until prey drifts within reach. This Trial translates that energy-thrifty waiting with an open mouth into ten still minutes holding an open bowl while pompoms drift down.

entries.title: Cram Fifteen Different Things Into One Jar
entries.objective: In one minute, stuff fifteen different kinds of object through the mouth of one wide jar.
entries.animalRule: Anything that fits through the mouth counts, but each must be a different kind of object, everything comes from the one room, and the gathering stops dead at sixty seconds.
entries.userBenefit: A frantic minute that ends in a very strange jar.
entries.mechanismConnection: Budgett's Frog — Water arrives • Eat everything • Breed at once: When rain refills the Chaco pools a Budgett's Frog emerges into a short window and takes almost anything that fits its enormous mouth, including insects, fish and other frogs, before the water disappears again. This Trial translates that indiscriminate feeding with a huge mouth inside a short window into a one-minute race to cram fifteen different kinds of object into one wide jar.

entries.title: Crawl a Plate Path Testing Every Plate
entries.objective: Cross a floor route of paper plates on all fours, keeping constant contact and testing each support before trusting it.
entries.animalRule: At least three of your hands and knees are on the floor at every moment, and no plate takes weight until it has been pressed.
entries.userBenefit: A gentle, absorbing movement game that trains careful footing.
entries.mechanismConnection: Potto — Gripping • Testing • Advancing: the potto moves hand over hand with several limbs always in contact, testing each branch before transferring weight onto it, because a fall or a rotten support in the dark canopy is too costly to risk. This Trial translates that constant contact and test-before-trust advance into a slow crawl that presses every plate before putting weight on it.

entries.title: Crawl Across Five Cushions Keeping Three Limbs Down
entries.objective: Cross a line of five floor cushions on hands and knees without ever lifting more than one limb at a time.
entries.animalRule: At least three limbs stay in contact with a cushion at every moment, and touching the floor means restarting.
entries.userBenefit: A slow, surprisingly demanding coordination challenge.
entries.mechanismConnection: Common Wall Gecko — Rhythmic • Anchored • Incremental: Tarentola mauritanica climbs walls on toe pads of microscopic setae that grip by van der Waals forces and peel off instantly, moving one foot at a time so at least two or three stay attached at every moment. This Trial translates that grip-and-release stepping that keeps most feet anchored into a cushion-to-cushion crawl that lifts only one limb at a time.

entries.title: Crawl Into Shared Hollow on Owl Cue
entries.objective: Build one low hollow with a single entrance and, when a random owl cue sounds, crawl into it with two others and rest there together for ten minutes.
entries.animalRule: One shelter with one entrance: all three share it, go in only on the owl cue, and stay settled inside for the full ten minutes.
entries.userBenefit: Ten cosy minutes with people you like.
entries.mechanismConnection: Cuban Hutia — Sheltering • Communal • Retreating: Capromys pilorides spends the day lying up in tree hollows, rock crevices or caves, often with several animals sharing one shelter, and retreats there when a boa, owl or dog approaches. This Trial translates that shared retreat into one crevice-like hollow into three people withdrawing together on an owl cue and resting there for ten minutes.

entries.title: Crawl Single File to Find Eight Hidden Toys
entries.objective: With at least one other person, crawl single file through a room of cushion cover and find eight hidden toys.
entries.animalRule: Stay low and in single file the whole time; the follower may search only where the leader has already been.
entries.userBenefit: A giggly, cooperative search that works for any age.
entries.mechanismConnection: Egyptian Mongoose — Foraging • Diurnal • Cover-bound: Herpestes ichneumon works low and nose-down through reedbeds, scrub and riverside thicket, digging and probing cover for small prey, and females with young often travel in single file. This Trial translates that low, probing search of dense cover in single file into a crawl through cushion cover finding eight toys.

entries.title: Create One Before-And-After Entrance
entries.objective: Film your ordinary look, then change one strong visual element and make a second entrance into the same room.
entries.animalRule: Feeds on fruit and insects and keeps a display court swept clear, looking like an unremarkable black bird. Keep that true for the whole attempt.
entries.userBenefit: Practises presentation and self-expression while producing a clear, entertaining transformation.
entries.mechanismConnection: Superb Bird-of-paradise expresses Stage Transformation through this mode: Superb Bird-of-paradise — Cape-Spread Ellipse Display — Foraging • Sweeping • Ordinary: Feeds on fruit and insects and keeps a display court swept clear, looking like an unremarkable black bird. The Trial carries that same limiting structure into one concrete human action.

entries.title: Create One Extra Grip Point
entries.objective: Use a clip, hook, edge, or other harmless external support to hold an awkward object steady while you complete one small task.
entries.animalRule: Your hands may not provide the missing grip once the task starts; the external support has to do that job.
entries.userBenefit: Improves tool use by outsourcing a physical limitation to the environment instead of forcing your body to compensate.
entries.mechanismConnection: Brown Shrike uses this mode by uses a thorn or wire as an external substitute for the gripping foot it does not have, so a songbird can dismember prey larger than a songbird should be able to handle and store what it cannot eat

entries.title: Create One Golden Entrance
entries.objective: Add one bold gold, yellow or bright element to your outfit and make a deliberately overconfident entrance into a room.
entries.animalRule: Returns daily to a traditional canopy tree where many males display together for visiting females. Keep that true for the whole attempt.
entries.userBenefit: Practises presence and playful confidence while producing instantly readable social proof.
entries.mechanismConnection: Greater Bird-of-paradise expresses Golden Presentation through this mode: Greater Bird-of-paradise — Canopy Lek Plume Raising — Attending • Displaying • Inherited: Returns daily to a traditional canopy tree where many males display together for visiting females. The Trial carries that same limiting structure into one concrete human action.

entries.title: Credited With More Than It Did
entries.objective: The Yellow Sac Spider is a small hunting spider that builds a silk retreat rather than a web, hunts foliage at night, and delivers a genuinely painful bite if pressed against skin. It has also been blamed for necrotic wounds across decades of medical literature on very thin evidence, and careful review has found the attribution largely unsupported. A real but modest effect became a reputation out of all proportion. Its principle is Silk Day-Cell. The metaphor? Check whether the thing you are blaming actually did it.
entries.animalRule: The attribution must be actually tested rather than reasoned about, and the conclusion has to be stated even if it clears the suspect.
entries.userBenefit: Blaming the wrong cause means you keep treating something that was never the problem while the real one continues. One test usually settles it in an afternoon.
entries.mechanismConnection: Cheiracanthium punctorium has been widely implicated in necrotic arachnidism, but systematic review of verified bites finds the association largely unsupported, with symptoms typically limited to transient local pain.

entries.title: Creep All the Way In, Then Once
entries.objective: The popeyed scorpionfish is a rarely seen ambush predator that barely moves. It creeps slowly towards prey using its fins, closing the distance over a long approach, and small fishes that come close enough are taken in a single sudden gulp. There is no chase and no second attempt, so the whole result rests on how patiently the approach was made. Its principle is Watchful Venom. The metaphor? Close the distance before you act.
entries.animalRule: The approach must be visibly unhurried, and the attempt happens only once with no second try afterwards.
entries.userBenefit: Attempting things from too far out means you get refused and then try again from a worse position. Closing the distance first turns one attempt into the only one you need.
entries.mechanismConnection: Rhinopias argoliba stalks prey with slow fin-driven creeping before a single rapid suction strike, a strategy with no capacity for pursuit.

entries.title: Creep One Taped Square Gathering Ten Pegs
entries.objective: Stay low on hands and knees inside a one-metre taped square and slowly gather ten scattered pegs into a bowl without ever crossing the tape.
entries.animalRule: Stay low and stay home: at least one knee and one hand always on the floor, and no part of you ever crosses the tape.
entries.userBenefit: A few minutes of slow, low, mindful movement with a clear finish.
entries.mechanismConnection: Common Musk Turtle — Cautious • Grounded • Local: Sternotherus odoratus is a poor swimmer that walks slowly along the bottom of shallow water, staying low and small within one small familiar patch rather than roaming. This Trial translates that slow, low bottom-walking within one small patch into creeping on hands and knees around a taped square to gather ten pegs.

entries.title: Creep Up and Strike One Paper Shrimp
entries.objective: Walk slowly up to a paper shrimp, then snatch it with one fast sticky-tipped strike.
entries.animalRule: Slow all the way to the line, then one fast strike only, with feet behind the line.
entries.userBenefit: A playful test of patience followed by speed.
entries.mechanismConnection: Flamboyant Cuttlefish — Walking • Hunting • Benthic: By day Metasepia pfefferi walks slowly over sand and mud on its lower arms and mantle flaps in dull mottled colours, then catches shrimps, crabs and small fish with a fast strike of its two tentacles, whose sucker-lined clubs grip the prey. This Trial translates that slow walk ending in a fast sucker-tipped tentacle strike into a slow approach ending in one sticky-tipped newspaper strike.

entries.title: Creep Up on One Hidden Warm Spot
entries.objective: Blindfolded, creep slowly up to a thin towel and mark the one warm spot a helper has hidden beneath it among cool decoys, in a single sweep.
entries.animalRule: A slow, low approach and a single sweep of the hand, with the blindfold on throughout and headphones on while the bags are placed: one pass, one coin.
entries.userBenefit: A calm, curious test of a sense you rarely notice you have.
entries.mechanismConnection: Common Vampire Bat — Stalking • Lapping • Heat-sensing: Desmodus rotundus approaches a sleeping animal slowly and low, often on the ground using its strong thumbs, and then pinpoints a spot where blood runs close to the skin with heat-sensitive pits around its nose leaf before making a small cut. This Trial translates that slow, low approach to a sleeping host and the heat-guided pinpointing of one spot into creeping up blindfolded on a thin towel and marking its one hidden warm spot in a single sweep.

entries.title: Crop a Plate of Peas With Lips Alone
entries.objective: Clear a plate of cooked peas using only your lips to gather them, hands behind your back.
entries.animalRule: Lips only: no hands, no fork and no licking the plate with your tongue.
entries.userBenefit: A daft, surprisingly tricky snack that makes you laugh at yourself.
entries.mechanismConnection: Common Hippopotamus — Walking out • Cropping short grass • Returning before dawn: A Common Hippopotamus leaves the water after dark and grazes short grass by cropping it with its broad, muscular lips rather than its enormous teeth, taking remarkably little food for its size. This Trial translates that lip-cropping of short grass rather than biting with the teeth into a plate of peas cleared with the lips alone.

entries.title: Crop Fast, Chew in the Shade
entries.objective: A banteng is a ruminant living where forest meets grassland, and that lets it split the job: crop grass quickly out in the clearing where it is exposed, then withdraw into the forest edge and spend the long hours processing it in shade and cover. The eating is fast and the digesting is slow and safe. Its principle is Tropical Wild Strength. The metaphor? Take it in fast where you are exposed, and do the slow work somewhere nobody can see you.
entries.animalRule: No processing may happen where the gathering occurred during the attempt, and the gathering has to be visibly quicker than the processing.
entries.userBenefit: Doing the slow thoughtful part where you are interrupted means it takes three times as long and still comes out badly. Taking it somewhere sheltered fixes both.
entries.mechanismConnection: Bos javanicus grazes rapidly in open clearings during cooler hours and retreats to forest edge cover to ruminate, minimising exposure time.

entries.title: Crop the Same Plot Again
entries.objective: The Green Sea Turtle is the only sea turtle that becomes herbivorous as an adult, and that runs through everything. It grazes seagrass meadows by cropping the same small plots repeatedly rather than moving on, which keeps the blades young, digestible and productive. It is closer to tending than to feeding, and it changes the meadow itself. Its principle is Natal Return. The metaphor? Stop looking for fresh ground. Go back over the same plot until it improves.
entries.animalRule: Nothing new may be started during the attempt, and the thing worked on must be something you have already made or used before. The improvement has to be visible.
entries.userBenefit: Starting fresh feels like progress and leaves you with a field of unfinished things. Going back over the same plot is what actually makes one of them good, and good is the only version anyone uses.
entries.mechanismConnection: Chelonia mydas adults graze seagrass by repeatedly cropping discrete plots rather than moving between areas, maintaining the sward in a young, nutrient-rich and highly productive state that supports their slow hindgut fermentation.

entries.title: Cross One Failed-Pool Route
entries.objective: Mark two 'water' zones with paper and move between them using only the dry spaces while carrying a small object.
entries.animalRule: You may not step inside either marked water zone; the carried object must arrive without being put down.
entries.userBenefit: Practises route adaptation when the obvious environment becomes unusable, while preserving the useful payload.
entries.mechanismConnection: African Sharptooth Catfish uses this mode by breathes air through branched arborescent organs above the gills, which lets it live in water that would suffocate other fish and move across wet ground when a pool fails

entries.title: Cross One Room Without Catching Light
entries.objective: Cross One Room Without Catching Light.
entries.animalRule: Any visible flash means restart from the beginning.
entries.userBenefit: You turn wing transparency into one concrete, visible experience instead of an abstract idea.
entries.mechanismConnection: Glasswing Butterfly — Drifting • Shaded • Unresolved: The butterfly flies steadily through the understory in daylight rather than hiding, relying on a wing surface that returns almost no highlight at any viewing angle so that movement never announces itself with a flash. This Trial translates that mid-frequency mechanism into one room avoiding light flashes.

entries.title: Cross One Room Without Heel Noise
entries.objective: Cross One Room Without Heel Noise.
entries.animalRule: If a heel makes an audible impact, restart from the beginning.
entries.userBenefit: You turn branch secrecy into one concrete experience with a visible finish.
entries.mechanismConnection: Spotted Linsang — Nocturnal • Sheathed • Weightless: Fully retractile claws stay sharp because they never touch the ground, and a body barely wider than the head moves along branches at night at under a kilogram. This Trial translates that mechanism into one room without heel noise.

entries.title: Cross One Sticky Route
entries.objective: Create a short route across a smooth surface using removable paper markers, then move an object along it without lifting it.
entries.animalRule: The object must stay in contact with the surface for the whole route and may only move along the marked path.
entries.userBenefit: Develops controlled movement through continuous contact, useful for handling awkward objects without losing grip.
entries.mechanismConnection: Red Slug uses this mode by uses a single mucus that switches between gluing and lubricating depending on whether it is being sheared, which lets the animal grip and slide on the same substance at the same time and climb surfaces it could not otherwise hold

entries.title: Cross One Sticky Zone Lightly
entries.objective: Cross One Sticky Zone Lightly.
entries.animalRule: Only the three marked squares may be touched; standing on any other ends the crossing.
entries.userBenefit: You cross using three contact points instead of six, which is a real change in how you move.
entries.mechanismConnection: Keeps almost all of its body clear of a surface that traps other insects by standing on very long thin legs and touching it at only a few small points, so a plant defence built to catch insects does not catch it

entries.title: Cross Six Steps on Separate Pads
entries.objective: Cross Six Steps on Separate Pads.
entries.animalRule: Use a clear level floor and non-slip pads; no jumping or running.
entries.userBenefit: You turn impossible timing into one concrete experience with a visible finish.
entries.mechanismConnection: Common Basilisk — Slapping • Stroking • Outpacing: Fleeing, it runs onto the water, each foot slapping down to make an air cavity and pushing off before the water closes over it. This Trial translates that mechanism into six steps across separate floor pads.

entries.title: Cross Ten Steps With Wide Arms
entries.objective: Cross Ten Steps With Wide Arms.
entries.animalRule: Feet must stop at all three marks before movement resumes.
entries.userBenefit: You turn highland agility into one concrete, visible experience instead of an abstract idea.
entries.mechanismConnection: Andean Lapwing — Running • Stopping • Picking: Broad rounded wings and a light body give very low wing loading, so the same unhurried wingbeat still generates lift in air holding roughly two thirds the density it has at sea level. This Trial translates that mid-frequency mechanism into ten steps with wide arms.

entries.title: Cross the Border in Numbers
entries.objective: Damselfish are among the most aggressive animals on a reef for their size: a resident holds a patch of algal turf, weeds it, fertilises it and attacks anything approaching, including fish many times its length. A single surgeonfish approaching is driven off every time. A shoal of fifty is not, because the defender cannot be everywhere, and the turf is grazed. Numbers, not strength. Its principle is Sand-Film Grazing. The metaphor? Alone you will be turned away. Go together and the refusal stops working.
entries.animalRule: At least two other people must make the same request within the same short window, agreed in advance rather than coincidentally.
entries.userBenefit: A request made alone is easy to refuse and you take it personally. The same request from three people at once is usually not refused at all.
